NUM_PET_ACTION_SLOTS = 10
-- ── The token icons ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- -- These are GLOBALS on purpose, and the names are a contract, not a choice: -- `GetPetActionInfo` hands back the NAME of one of them for a token slot and the paint -- below resolves it with getglobal — the reference's own convention, and the one -- `ui_pet/bar.rs` writes against. The icon paths are the reference's too; they name real -- .blp files in the install, so there is nothing to choose there either. -- -- What IS ours is the grouping. The bar's tokens come in two families and `ui_pet/bar.rs` -- already separates them at the seam that names these — `command_token` (the orders you -- give, keyed `PET_ACTION_*`) and `reaction_token` (the stance the pet holds, keyed -- `PET_MODE_*`) — so they are laid out in those two families, in that file's own order, -- and the two halves of the mapping read side by side. The reference keeps them in one -- undifferentiated block, which hides the split.
-- Commands — the four orders, in `ui_pet/bar.rs`'s `command_token` order. PET_WAIT_TEXTURE = "Interface\\Icons\\Spell_Nature_TimeStop" PET_FOLLOW_TEXTURE = "Interface\\Icons\\Ability_Tracking" PET_ATTACK_TEXTURE = "Interface\\Icons\\Ability_GhoulFrenzy" PET_DISMISS_TEXTURE = "Interface\\Icons\\Spell_Shadow_Teleport"
-- Reactions — the three stances, in `ui_pet/bar.rs`'s `reaction_token` order. PET_PASSIVE_TEXTURE = "Interface\\Icons\\Ability_Seal" PET_DEFENSIVE_TEXTURE = "Interface\\Icons\\Ability_Defend" PET_AGGRESSIVE_TEXTURE = "Interface\\Icons\\Ability_Racial_BloodRage"
-- ── The autocast sparkle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- -- The reference's "autocast is on" mark is a <Model> playing -- Interface\Buttons\UI-AutoCastButton.mdx, and what that model actually is came out of the -- shipped .m2 with `benilla-extract m2bones`/`m2part`: -- -- 4 bones, pivoting at the corners of a 0.02 x 0.02 unit square, each keyed with the -- SAME 5-key 2.000 s translation loop walking the square edge by edge (0.5 s per edge) — -- the four phase-shifted by one corner each, so they chase one another round it. The -- tracks are `interp == 1`, LINEAR (read at the bone record's M2Track word, not assumed): -- constant speed along each edge, no easing into the corners, which is what the walk -- below reproduces. -- 4 particle emitters, one per bone: 300/s, life 1.000 s, Add blend, unlit, texture -- Interface\Buttons\GlowStar.blp, size half-extent 0.005 -> 0.0015 -> 0.001 over life, -- colour (0.976,0.875,0.192,1) -> (0.996,0.945,0.745,1) -> (1,1,1,0). Its spline is one -- cubic Bezier segment whose 4 control points are ALL AT THE ORIGIN — checked, all four, -- because the two INTERIOR handles are what would bend the path and reading only the -- endpoints proves nothing — so a particle never travels: it is born where the bone is -- and shrinks away there. The effect is therefore four comet trails running round the -- button's rim, not a rotating ring. -- -- MODEL UNITS -> PIXELS is the widget's own projection, not a calibration -- (wow-re `system/ui/scratch/modelframe-animation-clock.md`, §1317's fold-back). There is -- no fixed px/unit: the ortho leg gives -- -- px per model unit = (5/3) * modelScale * layoutScale * screenHeightPx -- -- which in FrameXML units collapses to **1280 * modelScale * layoutScale**, independent of -- aspect and resolution. `scale="1.2"` on the ref's <Model> is SetModelScale, NOT -- Frame:SetScale (`0x76cb36`, stored at `+0x3a0`), so 1 model unit = 1536 FrameXML units -- and the 0.02 path is **30.72** across — 1.024x a 30-unit button, overhanging its top and -- right by 2.4%. The model ORIGIN is the frame rect's BOTTOM-LEFT, not its centre, which is -- why a square authored 0..0.02 lands across the whole button instead of in one quadrant. -- -- This corrects the 1200 px/unit figure this header carried until then, which was the right -- formula evaluated at a 720 px screen **with the 1.2 left out** — two errors that nearly -- cancelled (28.8 vs 30.72) and made the wrong number look like it cross-checked. BagFrame's -- Cooldown calibration is the same coincidence and is flagged there. -- -- OUR ONE DEPARTURE is the particle COUNT: 300 live per emitter is 12 000 quads across a -- full bar. We draw a SAMPLE of the same trail — each sample sits where the bone was `age` -- ago and reads the same position/size/colour ramps at that age — so the trail's shape, -- speed and colour are the file's; only its density is ours. -- -- **How many samples is DERIVED, not chosen** (B228). It was 8, evenly spaced in age, on -- the claim that the trail "reads identically at a fraction" of 300. Nobody had checked -- that claim, and the arithmetic says it is false. The rim is 4 x 30.72 = 122.9 px round -- and the lap is 2.0 s, so the bone travels 61.4 px/s and a particle's 1.0 s life spans -- 61.4 px of rim — two whole edges. Eight even samples therefore sit 7.7 px apart, while -- the stars behind the head are 4.6 px and then 3.1 px across: the back half of every trail -- was a row of SEPARATED DOTS where the file draws one continuous streak. Marching dots are -- legible motion in a way a smooth streak is not, so it read as speed on a loop that runs -- at the authored rate (nazriel, B228). -- -- So the samples are spaced by the file's own SIZE ramp rather than evenly: each step -- advances one star-width / OVERLAP of arc. That spends samples in the tail where the -- stars are small and saves them at the head where a 15 px star covers everything — -- continuous everywhere, and cheaper than a uniform spacing fine enough for the tail. BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PX_PER_UNIT = 1280 -- the ortho leg's BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_SCALE = 1.2 -- the ref Model's BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PERIOD = 2.0 -- seq0 loop, seconds BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_LIFE = 1.0 -- particle lifespan BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_EMITTERS = 4 -- Star-widths of cover on every point of the trail. 1 would put neighbours exactly edge to -- edge, and a GlowStar fades out toward its own edge, so the seam would show; 2 (centres -- half a width apart) is the cheapest value with no seam. BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_OVERLAP = 2 -- 0.02 units square, in pixels. BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_SIZE = 0.02 * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PX_PER_UNIT * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_SCALE -- Half-extent -> full width, in pixels: {0.005, 0.0015, 0.001} * 2 * K * scale. -- The MID key is 0.0015, not the 0.002 this table carried until B228: `m2part` printed the -- ramp at 3 decimals and rounded it up, and the transcription took the printout at its -- word. (Fixed at the instrument too — that column prints 4 decimals now.) 33% of the -- mid-life star, so the trail was reading thicker than the file authors it. BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_STAR = { 0.010 * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PX_PER_UNIT * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_SCALE, 0.003 * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PX_PER_UNIT * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_SCALE, 0.002 * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PX_PER_UNIT * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_SCALE, } -- The over-life colour ramp's three keys (the file's), as {r, g, b, a}. BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_COLOR = { {0.976, 0.875, 0.192, 1.0}, {0.996, 0.945, 0.745, 1.0}, {1.000, 1.000, 1.000, 0.0}, }
-- ── The widget's CLOCK, truncation and all ──────────────────────────────────────────── -- -- The reference does NOT play this loop at wall-clock rate, and that is the whole of what -- was left of B228. `CSimpleModel` overrides `CSimpleFrame`'s per-frame OnUpdate slot -- (vtable `0x81c608` idx14 -> `0x76d7f0`) and advances its private `CM2Scene` clock by -- `__ftol(elapsed * 1000.0)` — **truncated, with no fractional carry**. The WORLD's driver -- does the same conversion with a `+0.5` first (`0x48366b`); the widget path omits it -- (`0x76d846`). So the widget throws away `frac(elapsed * 1000)` every single frame, and a -- 2000 ms band takes `2000 * T / floor(T)` ms at frame time T ms: -- -- 30 fps -> 2020 ms · 60 fps -> 2083 ms · 75 fps -> 2051 · 144 fps -> 2315 -- -- It is **never faster than 2.000 s**. Our old exact-2.000 s clock was therefore faster -- than any real 1.12 client at any frame rate — the floor of the range rather than a point -- in it — which is exactly nazriel's "a bit too fast". (wow-re -- `system/ui/scratch/modelframe-animation-clock.md`, §5 cross-checked.) -- -- So the clock is an integer MILLISECOND counter here too, advanced the reference's way. -- This is the mechanism, not a tuned constant: it tracks the player's own frame rate the -- way theirs did. Two knowing limits. The reference's `elapsed` is an **f32**, so -- `f32(0.01) * 1000 = 9.99999978` truncates to 9 — a whole millisecond lost at a nominally -- clean frame rate, and the exact hazard the world path's `+0.5` cancels; we do not model -- f32 rounding, so we lose marginally less than it does. And above 1000 fps the reference -- freezes outright (every frame truncates to 0 ms) — reproduced rather than guarded, -- because a guard would be inventing behaviour, but no 2006 client ever reached it and a -- frozen sparkle at four-figure frame rates is this line's fault, not a new bug. BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PERIOD_MS = 2000
function BenillaPetAutocast_Advance(frame, elapsed) local ms = (frame.clock or 0) + math.floor(elapsed * 1000) frame.clock = math.mod(ms, BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PERIOD_MS) return frame.clock end
-- Where an emitter sits at lap fraction `f` (0..1), as an offset from the button's -- BOTTOMLEFT in pixels — the model's own origin (see the header), so this is the authored -- square placed exactly where the widget places it: 0..30.72 across a 30 px button, its -- corner on the button's corner, overhanging the top and right by 0.72 px. The bone tracks -- walk it clockwise on screen from that bottom-left corner, one edge per quarter-lap. function BenillaPetAutocast_Point(f) local s = BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_SIZE f = f - math.floor(f) -- wrap into 0..1 local edge = f * 4 local leg = math.floor(edge) local t = edge - leg -- 0..1 along this edge if leg == 0 then return 0, t * s -- bottom-left -> top-left elseif leg == 1 then return t * s, s -- top-left -> top-right elseif leg == 2 then return s, s - t * s -- top-right -> bottom-right else return s - t * s, 0 -- bottom-right -> bottom-left end end
-- Sample a 3-key over-life ramp (the M2's own {k0, k1 at mid, k2} shape, linear between). function BenillaPetAutocast_Ramp(keys, age) local a, b, t if age <= 0.5 then a, b, t = keys[1], keys[2], age * 2 else a, b, t = keys[2], keys[3], (age - 0.5) * 2 end if type(a) == "number" then return a + (b - a) * t end local out = {} for i = 1, table.getn(a) do out[i] = a[i] + (b[i] - a[i]) * t end return out end
-- The trail's sample AGES, walked once off the size ramp above (the header has the why). -- Each step advances by one local star-width / OVERLAP of rim, converted to seconds at the -- bone's own rim speed — so the spacing tightens as the stars shrink and the streak stays -- unbroken end to end. The count falls out of the file's numbers; nothing here picks it. function BenillaPetAutocast_TrailAges() local speed = 4 * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_SIZE / BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PERIOD -- px/s of rim local ages, age = {}, 0 while age < BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_LIFE do table.insert(ages, age) local w = BenillaPetAutocast_Ramp(BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_STAR, age / BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_LIFE) -- The step is only positive while the ramp is. This runs at FILE LOAD, so a future -- edit that put a zero in the size table would hang the whole UI before a frame -- ever drew — the failure mode decision 1306 exists for. Bail instead. if w <= 0 then break end age = age + w / BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_OVERLAP / speed end return ages end BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_AGES = BenillaPetAutocast_TrailAges() BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_TRAIL = table.getn(BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_AGES)
-- Build one button's sparkle pool: EMITTERS x TRAIL textures, hidden until autocast is on. -- -- Everything about a sample EXCEPT where it is right now is fixed by its age — size, -- colour and alpha are reads of the over-life ramps at an age that never changes for a -- given slot — so all of it is set HERE, once. The per-frame pass moves the texture and -- touches nothing else, which is why tripling the sample count still costs less per frame -- than the eight-sample version did (it re-derived all five values for every spark, every -- frame). Each spark also carries its fixed place in the loop: its emitter's quarter-lap -- offset, less how far the bone has moved on since this star was born. -- -- Built LAZILY, on the first frame the button actually autocasts. Most never do, and a -- pool that is only ever hidden is pure cost — 22 buttons' worth of it across the bar and -- the spell book. function BenillaPetAutocast_Create(button) button.sparks = {} for e = 0, BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_EMITTERS - 1 do for k = 1, BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_TRAIL do local age = BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_AGES[k] local life = age / BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_LIFE local size = BenillaPetAutocast_Ramp(BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_STAR, life) local c = BenillaPetAutocast_Ramp(BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_COLOR, life) local spark = button:CreateTexture(nil, "OVERLAY") spark:SetTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\GlowStar") spark:SetBlendMode("ADD") spark:SetWidth(size) spark:SetHeight(size) spark:SetVertexColor(c[1], c[2], c[3]) spark:SetAlpha(c[4]) spark:Hide() spark.phase = e / BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_EMITTERS - age / BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PERIOD table.insert(button.sparks, spark) end end end
-- Advance one button's sparkles to the bar's shared clock. Shared on purpose: the four -- emitters are one model, and every autocasting button plays the same loop in step, which -- is what the reference's per-button Models do too (each starts at sequence time 0 and -- they never drift, the loop being exact). -- -- Show and hide are EDGE work, not per-frame work: this runs for all ten buttons every -- frame and all but one or two of them are dark, so the old unconditional Hide loop was -- spending most of the bar's frame budget re-hiding what was already hidden. function BenillaPetAutocast_Update(button, clockMs) if not button.autocasting then if button.sparksLit then for i = 1, table.getn(button.sparks) do button.sparks[i]:Hide() end button.sparksLit = nil end return end if not button.sparks then BenillaPetAutocast_Create(button) end local sparks = button.sparks local lap = clockMs / BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PERIOD_MS for i = 1, table.getn(sparks) do local spark = sparks[i] -- SetPoint on the SAME point replaces it, so no ClearAllPoints is needed. The -- anchor is the button's BOTTOMLEFT because that is the model's own origin. local x, y = BenillaPetAutocast_Point(lap + spark.phase) spark:SetPoint("CENTER", button, "BOTTOMLEFT", x, y) end if not button.sparksLit then for i = 1, table.getn(sparks) do sparks[i]:Show() end button.sparksLit = 1 end end
-- ── The buttons ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
function BenillaPetActionButton_OnLoad(button, index) -- Ref PetActionButton_OnLoad l.234-235. The right-click registration is load-bearing, -- not boilerplate: it is the whole autocast toggle, and without it a right click is -- simply never delivered. button:RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp", "RightButtonUp") -- The drag trio (decision 1010). Both buttons drag, ref-verbatim -- (PetActionButton_OnLoad l.234) — and unlike the action bar's, ALL THREE gestures here -- reach the same verb: the reference's OnClick-under-shift, OnDragStart and -- OnReceiveDrag all call PickupPetAction, which forks on whether the cursor is already -- carrying. Both drag ends honour LOCK_ACTIONBAR since 1136 — the same uvar the main bar -- declares (ActionBar.xml), which is the ref's own arrangement too: PetActionBarFrame.lua -- reads a global UIOptionsFrame owns. button:RegisterForDrag("LeftButton", "RightButton") button.index = index button.icon = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Icon") button.cooldown = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Cooldown") button.autocastable = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "AutoCastable") -- No sparkle pool here: BenillaPetAutocast_Update builds it on the first frame this -- button actually autocasts, and most buttons never do. end
-- Ref PetActionButton_OnClick. The CheckButton widget toggles itself BEFORE OnClick fires, -- and the reference immediately clears that (`this:SetChecked(0)`) — nothing about this bar -- is locally latched, because the server owns every bit of it. Left = run the slot, unless -- the pet is already on the attack, in which case it calls off; right = flip autocast. function PetActionButton_OnClick(mouseButton) local button = this button:SetChecked(0) -- Shift outranks the button fork entirely (ref l.253-255): a shift-click on the pet bar -- is a pick-up whichever mouse button it came from, and it never toggles autocast. if IsShiftKeyDown() then PickupPetAction(button.index) PetActionBar_Update() elseif mouseButton == "RightButton" then TogglePetAutocast(button.index) elseif IsPetAttackActive(button.index) then PetStopAttack() else CastPetAction(button.index) end end
-- The KEYBIND pair (decision 1052) — ref PetActionButtonDown/Up l.218-231, which is where -- the BONUSACTIONBUTTONn bindings land: their bodies call BonusActionButtonDown/Up, and -- those are one-liners onto these (BonusActionBarFrame.lua:106-112). The ref's own -- runOnUp shape: DOWN only shows the pushed art, UP fires. -- -- Note what the key path does NOT do — it is a bare CastPetAction, with none of the click -- path's forks: no shift pick-up, no right-button autocast, and no IsPetAttackActive -- call-off. That is the reference's split, not a simplification of ours: the fork lives in -- PetActionButton_OnClick, which a key press never reaches. -- -- On a PET bar none of that is visible, because the call-off fork is DEAD CODE there: -- IsPetAttackActive needs the [0xb714b0] latch, and `0x4bd420` raises it only when the -- bar's unit is the one you are POSSESSING (ui_pet.rs's `possessing` carries the carve — -- UNIT_FLAG_POSSESSED, never a hunter's or warlock's pet). A pet's Attack button can never -- latch lit, so click and key both simply order the attack. The split is visible on a -- POSSESS bar (Mind Control, Eye of Kilrogg, Eyes of the Beast): there a click sends -- PetStopAttack and CTRL-1 re-issues the order instead. function PetActionButtonDown(id) local button = getglobal("PetActionButton" .. id) if ( button:GetButtonState() == "NORMAL" ) then button:SetButtonState("PUSHED") end end
function PetActionButtonUp(id) local button = getglobal("PetActionButton" .. id) if ( button:GetButtonState() == "PUSHED" ) then button:SetButtonState("NORMAL") CastPetAction(id) end end
-- Both drag ends are the SAME verb (ref l.269-283, byte-verified at `0x4be180`): with an -- empty cursor it picks the slot up, with a pet payload already held it drops onto this -- slot. There is no separate "place" binding on this bar, which is also why a spell or an -- item can never land here — nothing but a pet slot produces the payload it accepts. -- -- Both also honour the lock (the ref wraps each body in `if LOCK_ACTIONBAR ~= "1" then …`). -- The shift-click in OnClick above is unguarded on this bar too, exactly as the reference -- leaves it (l.253-255): the lock stops the drag, shift-click stays the way through. function PetActionButton_OnDragStart() local button = this if LOCK_ACTIONBAR == "1" then return end PickupPetAction(button.index) PetActionBar_Update() end
function PetActionButton_OnReceiveDrag() local button = this if LOCK_ACTIONBAR == "1" then return end PickupPetAction(button.index) PetActionBar_Update() end
-- Ref PetActionButton_OnEnter (PetActionBarFrame.lua l.285-305). ONE predicate, -- `isToken or UberTooltips == "0"`, decides two things at once: -- -- * WHICH TOOLTIP. A token slot has no spell to look up, so its tooltip is built here out -- of the two strings the info call already returned — and the BINDING (B230). Anything -- else is a real pet SPELL and goes through the engine's tooltip channel, which appends -- nothing. So the parenthesised key belongs to Attack/Follow/Stay and the reactions, and -- NOT to the pet's own spells: putting it on every slot would be the wrong fix. -- * WHERE IT SITS. Only the UberTooltips-off leg moves the tooltip beside the button -- (ANCHOR_RIGHT); a token with the CVar on, and every spell, take the default corner. -- The CVar registers "1" (cvars.rs carries the byte-read), so the off leg is the -- player's to reach and not what ships. -- -- The suffix is the ref's own expression and it is UNCONDITIONAL — no `if the key exists` -- guard, unlike MicroButtonTooltipText's version of the same idea (MicroMenu.xml). That is -- visible, not academic: GetBindingText answers "" for a nil key (UIParent.xml, transcribed -- from the ref's own l.1819-1821), so 1.12 really does render "Attack ()" on a token slot -- whose row is unbound. Stock, none are: BONUSACTIONBUTTON1-10 default to CTRL-1..CTRL-0 -- (bindings/commands.rs, byte-real from the install's bindings-cache.wtf). -- -- Those same ten rows are the binding B218 found the CORNER hotkey glyph can never show -- (the header's ref-divergence list has the `bindingSuffix == this:GetID()` string-vs-number -- reason). Corner empty, tooltip parenthesised — both faithful, at once. function PetActionButton_OnEnter() local button = this if not GameTooltip then return end -- engine tests load file subsets if not button.tooltipName then return end local uber = GetCVar("UberTooltips") if button.isToken or uber == "0" then if uber == "0" then GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") else GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor(GameTooltip, button) end local key = GetBindingText(GetBindingKey("BONUSACTIONBUTTON" .. button.index), "KEY_") GameTooltip:SetText(button.tooltipName .. NORMAL_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. " (" .. key .. ")" .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) if button.tooltipSubtext then GameTooltip:AddLine(button.tooltipSubtext, "", 0.5, 0.5, 0.5) end GameTooltip:Show() else GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor(GameTooltip, button) GameTooltip:SetPetAction(button.index) end end
function PetActionButton_OnLeave() local button = this if GameTooltip then GameTooltip:Hide() end end
-- ── The bar ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Ref PetActionBar_Update + PetActionBar_UpdateCooldowns, fused (one refresh event, see the -- header). Every branch below is the reference's, including the two that are easy to lose: -- an unnamed slot HIDES its button, and a slot with no texture swaps the button's ring from -- the filled UI-Quickslot2 to the empty UI-Quickslot. function PetActionBar_Update() local usable = GetPetActionsUsable() for i = 1, NUM_PET_ACTION_SLOTS do local button = getglobal("PetActionButton" .. i) local name, subtext, texture, isToken, isActive, autoCastAllowed, autoCastEnabled = GetPetActionInfo(i) button.isToken = isToken button.tooltipSubtext = subtext if isToken then -- The token convention: what came back are the NAMES of globals. button.icon:SetTexture(getglobal(texture)) button.tooltipName = getglobal(name) else button.icon:SetTexture(texture) button.tooltipName = name end
if isActive then button:SetChecked(1) else button:SetChecked(0) end if autoCastAllowed then button.autocastable:Show() else button.autocastable:Hide() end button.autocasting = autoCastEnabled
-- An unnamed slot hides — UNLESS the drop grid is up, which is the whole point of -- the grid: while a pet action rides the cursor every slot shows, so you can see -- where it may land (ref PetActionBar_Update l.122-128 + PetActionBar_ShowGrid). if name or (PetActionBarFrame.showgrid or 0) > 0 then button:Show() else button:Hide() end
if texture then SetDesaturation(button.icon, not usable and 1 or nil) button.icon:Show() button:SetNormalTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\UI-Quickslot2") else button.icon:Hide() button:SetNormalTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\UI-Quickslot") end
local start, duration, enable = GetPetActionCooldown(i) CooldownFrame_SetTimer(button.cooldown, start, duration, enable) end end
function PetActionBar_OnLoad() local frame = this frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD") frame:RegisterEvent("PET_BAR_UPDATE") -- The drop grid (decision 1010). A counter rather than a flag, ref-verbatim -- (PetActionBar_ShowGrid/_HideGrid): our engine derives the pair off one payload edge -- so they strictly alternate, but the counter is what the reference keeps and it costs -- nothing to keep it too. frame:RegisterEvent("PET_BAR_SHOWGRID") frame:RegisterEvent("PET_BAR_HIDEGRID") frame.showgrid = 0 frame.clock = 0 PetActionBar_OnEvent() end
-- The bar exists exactly while PetHasActionBar() does. Its show/hide re-fires the managed -- bottom-stack pass (UIParent.xml, decision 0272) — the pet term of that stack is what -- lifts the cast bar and the chat frame clear of it, which is the ref's own -- PetActionBarFrame.xml:205-210. -- Declares nothing and reads the ambient `event`, exactly as the reference does -- (PetActionBarFrame.lua:33 / .xml's bare `PetActionBar_OnEvent();`). PetActionBar_OnLoad's -- own tail call therefore lands with `event` nil, which is the no-grid-edge path — the same -- thing the old explicit `eventName` argument did when omitted. function PetActionBar_OnEvent() local frame = this if event == "PET_BAR_SHOWGRID" then frame.showgrid = frame.showgrid + 1 elseif event == "PET_BAR_HIDEGRID" and frame.showgrid > 0 then frame.showgrid = frame.showgrid - 1 end if PetHasActionBar() then PetActionBar_Update() frame:Show() else frame:Hide() end end
-- The shared sparkle clock. One OnUpdate for the whole bar rather than ten: the four -- emitters are one looping model, so every autocasting button is in step by construction. function BenillaPetActionBar_OnUpdate(frame, elapsed) local clockMs = BenillaPetAutocast_Advance(frame, elapsed) for i = 1, NUM_PET_ACTION_SLOTS do BenillaPetAutocast_Update(getglobal("PetActionButton" .. i), clockMs) end end
-- ── The pet menu's two dialogs (ref StaticPopup.lua l.738-748 + l.1069-1102 + l.365-374, -- decision 1066) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- They live here rather than with the rows that raise them (UnitPopup.xml) for the same -- reason every other dialog in this codebase lives with its arc's frame file: registering -- into StaticPopupDialogs is a LOAD-TIME dependency on UiPanels.xml's engine, and -- UnitPopup.xml is a shared engine that eight isolation prefixes load without it. Raising -- them is not a dependency — StaticPopup_Show resolves at click time. -- -- ABANDON_PET is the plain confirm. RENAME_PET is a CHAIN of two, which is the reference's -- own shape and not a flourish: the first collects the name, the second reads it back -- ("Name your pet 'Bruce'?") before anything is sent — because a rename is one-shot, so a -- typo is permanent in exactly the way the abandon is. That second Show happens while the -- first dialog is still up, which is why the engine's two instances are both needed. StaticPopupDialogs["ABANDON_PET"] = { text = ABANDON_PET, button1 = OKAY, button2 = CANCEL, OnAccept = function() PetAbandon(); end, timeout = 0, exclusive = 1, hideOnEscape = 1, }
